Issue 3066 asks for DXC's disassembly listing to print decoded, human-readable
forms where it currently prints raw values. Read the listing text, not the exit
status: every pane compiles successfully.

Read this caveat first. Compiler Explorer appends debug-info flags to every DXC
pane whatever arguments are given, which you can confirm in the dx.source.args
metadata node at the bottom of a DXC pane. So these panes show DXC at its most
readable, not its default. A plain command line without debug info prints less
than you see here: no per-instruction source location, and numbered SSA values
in place of the value names derived from resource declarations. Those same
flags also embed this file, comments and all, into a metadata node at the
bottom of each pane, so search the instruction listing by eye rather than by
text search.

In the DXC panes, three places.

First, the line calling dx.op.binary.f32. Two of its arguments are the operands
of the max(); one is a floating-point constant that the listing leaves in
LLVM's hexadecimal form. The trailing comment on that line decodes the opcode
number to a name and lists the operand names, then stops. That comment is the
one the issue quotes, and the issue's second request is for it to also carry
the constant in decimal.

Second, the line calling dx.op.bufferStore.f32. Its trailing comment ends at
the operand-name list, so the comment itself never says which of the four rows
of the Resource Bindings table further up the listing is being written; the
issue's fourth request is for that name to appear there. In these panes the
handle argument does carry a value name derived from the resource declaration,
because of the debug-info flags described above. The same applies to the
dx.op.sample.f32 and dx.op.cbufferLoadLegacy.f32 lines.

Third, the ViewId state block in the comment header, in the rows reading
"output N depends on inputs". Both sides of that relation are printed as bare
scalar element indices rather than as signature element names, and the
debug-info flags make no difference to them. That is the issue's last request.

The two panes are Compiler Explorer's oldest DXC and its trunk build. They
print the same text, so nothing in this range of versions has changed the
listing in the places above.
